What is the $y$-intercept of the parabola shown above?
questions.worked_solution:
First, we need to find the equation of the parabola. From the diagram, we see that the parabola has a vertex at $(2,-5)$ and passes through the point $(-2,3).$

The general standard equation of an up- or down-opening parabola with vertex at $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
(x-h)^{2}=4p(y-k),
$$

and substituting $(h,k)=(2,-5)$ into the above gives

$$
(x-2)^{2}=4p(y+5).
$$

Now, we need to find $p.$ Since the parabola passes through the point $(-2,3),$ we substitute $x=-2$ and $y=3$ into the equation and get

$$
\begin{aligned}(-2-2)^{2} & =4p(3+5) \\ 16 & =4p(8) \\ p & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the parabola is

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-2)^{2} & =2(y+5).\end{aligned}
$$

When the parabola intersects the $y$-axis, we must have $x=0.$ So, we substitute $x=0$ into the equation of the parabola and solve for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(0-2)^{2} & =2(y+5) \\ 4 & =2(y+5) \\ y & =2-5 \\ y & =-3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the $y$-intercept is $-3.$

The general standard equation of an up- or down-opening parabola with vertex $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
(x-h)^{2}=4p(y-k).
$$

Substituting $(h,k)=(-1,3)$ into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+1)^{2} & =4p(y-3).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we need to find $p.$ Since the parabola passes through the point $(-2,\frac{5}{2}),$ we substitute $x=-2$ and $y=\frac{5}{2}$ into the equation and get

$$
\begin{aligned}(-2+1)^{2} & =4p(\frac{5}{2}-3) \\ (-1)^{2} & =4p(-\frac{1}{2}) \\ 1 & =-2p \\ p & =-\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the parabola is

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+1)^{2} & =-2(y-3).\end{aligned}
$$

When the parabola intersects the $x$-axis, we must have $y=0.$ So, we substitute $y=0$ into the equation of the parabola and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+1)^{2} & =-2(0-3) \\ (x+1)^{2} & =6 \\ x+1 & =\pm \sqrt{6} \\ x & =-1\pm \sqrt{6}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, from left to right, the $x$-intercepts are $-1-\sqrt{6}$ and $-1+\sqrt{6}.$

The general standard equation of a left- or right-opening parabola with vertex at $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
(y-k)^{2}=4p(x-h),
$$

and substituting $(h,k)=(-8,-1)$ into the above gives

$$
(y+1)^{2}=4p(x+8).
$$

Now, we need to find $p.$ Since the parabola passes through the point $(-6,1),$ we substitute $x=-6$ and $y=1$ into the equation and get

$$
\begin{aligned}(1+1)^{2} & =4p(-6+8) \\ 4 & =4p(2) \\ p & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the parabola is

$$
\begin{aligned}(y+1)^{2} & =2(x+8).\end{aligned}
$$

When the parabola intersects the $y$-axis, we must have $x=0.$ So, we substitute $x=0$ into the equation of the parabola and solve for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(y+1)^{2} & =2(0+8) \\ (y+1)^{2} & =16 \\ y+1 & =\pm \sqrt{16} \\ y & =\pm 4-1 \\ y & =-5,3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, from top to bottom, the $y$-intercepts are $3$ and  $-5.$
